newsitem.title: USA: Flavored coffees help perk up specialty market.
newsitem.headline: Flavored coffees help perk up specialty market.

text.p: Many coffee connoisseurs would never be caught sipping a cup of vanilla nut creme, but specialty roasters say flavored coffees have become an important part of their business.

Coffee Roasters of New Orleans' roastmaster and production manager Bob Arceneaux estimated flavored coffees represent at least 30 percent of specialty sales industry-wide. In his company, they account for as much as 45 percent of sales. And a review by trade journal Tea & Coffee estimated flavored coffee holds a 55 percent share of all specialty coffee purchases in the U.S.
While some specialty roasters downplay the significance of the sector, Arceneaux said flavored coffees benefit the industry by attracting novice drinkers.
"Flavored coffee is the door which new customers come in," said Arceneaux. "People don't jump in and just drink Sumatra. They start with flavored coffee and graduate to premium coffee."
Arceneaux was among the 8,000 trade professionals attending the Specialty Coffee Association of America's 9th annual convention and exhibition April 18-21 in New Orleans.
To make flavored coffees, roasters generally use a less expensive mild arabica coffee since a premium bean's unique characteristics are often masked by the flavor.

The whole beans are roasted and tumbled with liquid flavoring while still warm since the flavoring is more readily passed through a porous surface. As the beans cool, the pores close and encapsulate the flavor beneath the surface.

Wolfgang Boehmer, the executive vice president and chief operating officer of Melchers Flavors of America Inc., which has been in the U.S. coffee-flavoring business since 1982 and has flavored teas for 30 years, said the flavoring business has experienced tremendous growth and should continue to boom.
"There is still the potential to grow above 10 percent a year," Boehmer said.
What are the best selling flavored coffees? Boehmer said Melchers most popular flavors -- out of some 2,500 -- are irish cream, hazelnut cream and vanilla.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity desk
